objective: Keep the validated 10-Core / one-shared-250-USDC product untouched as the primary engine, and independently develop five Satellite strategies for SUIUSDC, NEARUSDC, UNIUSDC, AAVEUSDC and BCHUSDC from the original Hixton V1/DMS_V1 basis so they can monetize as much as possible of the Core engine's approximately 90% idle time without reducing Core performance.
priorities: Run bounded independent V1-derived evolution for SUI/NEAR/UNI/AAVE/BCH using only the first two years of proxy history for selection.
Do not use old Core-V6 Satellite profiles as strategy seeds.
For each market compare unchanged V1 against bounded V1-derived probes for after-cost PnL, completed cycles, median hold and profit per occupied hour.
Select independently per market on training only; the five markets may end with different profiles.
Use the final one-year direct-USDC window only as a rejection gate; never retune from holdout outcomes.
Advance only holdout-positive candidates to the exact protected-Core idle-mask shared-250 replay.
Treat the owner's ~90% Core-idle figure as opportunity pool, not a quota; never sacrifice shared after-cost equity for utilization.
research_fronts: clean unchanged V1 baseline on SUI/NEAR/UNI/AAVE/BCH
bounded per-market V1 evolution without Core-V6 template inheritance
short-horizon exits and handoff only after the five Satellite entry/exit strategies themselves are suitable
success_rule: Mission success requires five independently developed Satellite-V1 profiles (or fewer if evidence rejects a market) that, together in one shared 250-USDC account, materially monetize protected Core idle time and improve or preserve after-cost baseline/stress shared equity with zero unacceptable Core opportunity displacement. The ~90% idle interval is the opportunity pool, not a quota that may override profitability or safety.

profit_concession.note: For the final satellite/router architecture, higher activity is not allowed to buy lower robust shared-account profit. Research diagnostics may explore trade-offs, but promotion requires non-regressive baseline and stress performance.
